sources.title: xAI docs full corpus (fetched 2026-08-26)
sources.what_it_established: Everything above, read from the vendor's own machine-readable docs dump rather than a rendered page; also that rate limits are published for text and embedding models only, with "For increases to Voice and Imagine API limits, contact sales@x.ai"

sources.title: In-repo capture of GET /v1/tts/voices (tier: vendor API response, captured by this estate)
sources.what_it_established: 72 voices across 20 language keys plus a multilingual pool: zh-CN ru it hi fr es da vi en sv-SE fi tr ja ko pt nl pl th ar de. This disagrees with the docs table in both directions — it adds da, sv-SE, fi, nl, pl, th and omits bn, id.

welsh.evidence: The docs supported-language table lists exactly 20 codes — auto, en, ar-EG, ar-SA, ar-AE, bn, zh, fr, de, hi, id, it, ja, ko, pt-BR, pt-PT, ru, es-MX, es-ES, tr, vi — with no cy. The in-repo capture of GET /v1/tts/voices has 21 keys and no Welsh either. The docs add one escape clause: "The model is also capable of generating speech in additional languages beyond those listed above, with varying degrees of accuracy."
welsh.rationale: Welsh is not claimed by the docs table and not present in the voice catalogue. The escape clause is explicitly quality-caveated and is not a support claim, and gate zero asks for CONVINCING Welsh. Note this costs the migration nothing: the Welsh courses have never been xAI-voiced — they run Azure plus human recordings from Aran and Catrin, and services/tts-service.cjs:217-222 hard-blocks any TTS at all for cym_n_for_eng and cym_s_for_eng.

languages_supported: docs table (20 codes): auto, en, ar-EG, ar-SA, ar-AE, bn, zh, fr, de, hi, id, it, ja, ko, pt-BR, pt-PT, ru, es-MX, es-ES, tr, vi
GET /v1/tts/voices catalogue as captured in tools/pod-voices-xai.json (21 keys, 72 voices): multilingual, zh-CN, ru, it, hi, fr, es, da, vi, en, sv-SE, fi, tr, ja, ko, pt, nl, pl, th, ar, de
built-in voice ids: eve (default), ara, leo, rex, sal — case-insensitive
version_pinning: NONE, and worse than none: there is no model identifier to pin. POST /v1/tts takes text, voice_id, language, output_format, speed and a few flags — there is no model_id field at all, so the synthesis model is unnamed, unversioned and unpinnable by the customer. xAI publishes no deprecation or notice policy for TTS voices, and the models page shows it does retire voice models when it wants to (grok-voice-think-fast-1.0 is marked Deprecated). The docs themselves concede output variability in the pronunciation section: left without a replacement rule, the model "spells these out, and not the same way twice". That sentence is the incumbent admitting nondeterminism in its own documentation. The honest framing for the report is therefore: on axis E and axis F we are not giving anything up, because we never had it.
cloning_consent: No consent mechanism is documented. Custom Voices is described as "Clone a voice from a short reference clip" with recording-quality advice and no verification step, no consent statement, no attestation tickbox mentioned in the API docs. The only gate is geographic — "Custom Voices is currently only available in the United States, with the exception of Illinois" — which reads as a response to Illinois biometric-privacy law rather than a consent design. API creation (POST /v1/custom-voices) is Enterprise-only; the console allows 30 free custom voices. Reference clips are capped at 120 seconds, 90+ recommended.

controls.temperature: None. No temperature, top_p or sampling control is exposed.
controls.other: speed 0.7-1.5 (default 1.0). replace — a validated map of phrase to spoken substitution, accepting either respellings or IPA between slashes, which the docs say "makes the reading deterministic" for that phrase. text_normalization (default false). with_timestamps returning character-level start/end times in a JSON envelope. optimize_streaming_latency 0-2. Inline speech tags in the text: [pause], [laugh] and wrapping tags <whisper>, <emphasis>, <slow>. Output format object: codec mp3/wav/pcm/mulaw/alaw, sample rates to 48 kHz, bit rate. 15,000-character cap on the unary endpoint; a WebSocket streaming endpoint exists at wss://api.x.ai/v1/tts.

self_host: No. Cloud API only, no container, no weights.
pricing: $15.00 per 1M characters — identical to Azure S1 neural, and roughly one seventh of ElevenLabs v3. Custom voice creation is free in the console (30 voices).
rate_limits: Not published for the Voice API. The rate-limits page covers text and embedding models only and says: "For increases to Voice and Imagine API limits, contact sales@x.ai". What we know instead comes from our own production defence: XAI_TTS_CONCURRENCY defaults to 4 (services/tts-service.cjs:51) and there is a circuit breaker that pauses xAI renders for 60s when more than 4% of the last 50 responses come back as inaudible stubs (services/tts-service.cjs:128-160). 429 and 408 are treated as transient and retried (services/tts-service.cjs:542).

files: services/voicelab/params.cjs:26 (Tom's clone gfzdpspr5fdp), :66-84 (voice menu from the catalogue)
live_integration.endpoint: POST https://api.x.ai/v1/tts, Authorization: Bearer $XAI_API_KEY, Content-Type: application/json (services/tts-service.cjs:449). Metadata reads at GET https://api.x.ai/v1/tts/voices/{voice_id} (tools/xai-voice-metadata-sync.cjs:15).
live_integration.settings_we_send: { text, voice_id, language, output_format: { codec: "mp3", sample_rate: 24000, bit_rate: 128000 } } and nothing else (services/tts-service.cjs:436-445). voice_id is passed through verbatim and may be a preset (eve|ara|leo|rex|sal) or a custom clone id such as gfzdpspr5fdp; an "xai_" storage prefix is stripped only in the VoiceLab list builder (services/voicelab/params.cjs:102), never on the render path (services/voice-config-service.cjs:474). language is a BCP-47 steer, defaulting to "auto" — and the code warns on auto because the multilingual voices are English-dominant and read cross-language words with English phonology under auto (services/tts-service.cjs:425-430, ita pilot 2026-07-10). Text cap 15,000 enforced locally at :421.
live_integration.determinism_notes: Three of the vendor's determinism-relevant parameters are documented and we send none of them. (1) `speed` exists at 0.7-1.5 — the code comment at services/tts-service.cjs:432 says "xAI currently does not document a speed parameter on the /v1/tts endpoint" and routes speed through downstream mastering instead; the vendor docs now document it, so that comment is stale and the estate is re-timing audio in post that could be asked for directly. (2) `replace` gives an IPA pronunciation override the docs describe as making the reading deterministic — we never use it, so every proper noun and loanword is at the model's discretion on every render. (3) `with_timestamps` returns character-level timings — the code comment at :405 says "Word boundaries are null - xAI does not provide them" and returns null, which is why xAI clips lack the boundary data Azure clips carry. There is no seed and no temperature to omit. The estate's actual defence against xAI nondeterminism is not a parameter at all: it is a whisper-based phonology gate that re-rolls any non-English render whose DETECTED spoken language comes back English (services/tts-service.cjs:563-700), which only exists because xAI renders the same steered text in the wrong phonology often enough to need catching.

gaps: xAI publishes no rate limits for the Voice API. Everything quoted here about throughput is our own empirical defence, not a vendor figure.
xAI publishes no deprecation or notice policy for TTS voices or the TTS model, and no model identifier exists to pin. There is nothing to cite because there is nothing published.

The docs supported-language table and the GET /v1/tts/voices catalogue DISAGREE. The catalogue has Danish, Swedish, Finnish, Dutch, Polish and Thai voices that the docs table omits; the docs table has Bengali and Indonesian that the catalogue omits. The catalogue in tools/pod-voices-xai.json is a capture, not a live read — it was not refreshed in this pass because that would mean calling the API.

Estate use is not the same as vendor support. pdc (Pennsylvania Dutch) appears in the migration scope but is claimed by no vendor anywhere and is not a language any of the three lists; pdc_for_eng is in fact hard-blocked from TTS in services/tts-service.cjs:217-222 as a human-voice course (Tom's ruling 2026-08-14). Treat pdc as 0/3 on this board, not as an xAI capability.

No quality BENCHMARK for xAI was found — only marketing copy ("a rich set of expressive voices", "high-fidelity"). The claim that xAI is our quality bar rests on this estate's own listening, not on a published evaluation. That is worth stating plainly in the report: we are moving off a benchmark nobody has measured.
Custom Voices being US-only excluding Illinois was not chased to a licence or terms document; whether a UK-based team may lawfully create and use xAI custom voices at all was not established.
